dossier.summary: Tessera Labs sells sample and reagent inventory software to biotech labs. It maps freezers shelf by shelf and sends reorder alerts. The product tour names Halden Bio as a customer.
dossier.why_now: Hired a VP of Marketing in September.

data.headline: Tessera's homepage talks to IT, but the buyer is the lab manager
data.summary: The product tour is good: real screens, a freezer map, a reorder alert. The words around it are written for an IT buyer, so the lab manager who signs off on this has to translate.

findings.quote: Next-generation inventory intelligence for modern life sciences organizations.
findings.cost: A lab manager still doesn't know if it tracks samples, reagents or both. They came with a freezer problem and the headline doesn't mention one.

findings.quote: Unify your data, eliminate silos and accelerate discovery with a robust, scalable platform.
findings.cost: These are IT words. The person who loses an afternoon hunting for a reagent lot doesn't see their problem here.
It sounds like a waitlist. A manager comparing three tools picks the one they can look at today.
The tour names Halden Bio. One named lab with one result would do more than this line.

rewrites.before: Next-generation inventory intelligence for modern life sciences organizations.
rewrites.after: Know where every sample and reagent is, down to the freezer shelf.
rewrites.why: The lab manager sees their own Monday morning in the first line.

rewrites.before: Unify your data, eliminate silos and accelerate discovery with a robust, scalable platform.
rewrites.after: Scan it in, find it later, reorder before it runs out.
rewrites.why: Three things a lab does every week, in the order they happen.
They know they can look around today, without waiting on anyone.

next_steps: Put Halden Bio's name and one result right next to the product tour.
Caption the freezer map screen with what the lab manager is looking at.
